assign.request: For every concern in the platform brief, what does this framework already have - reuse as-is, extend, or missing? And which topic abstraction is cleanest: Topic extends Page, an is: topic role, or plain config.

log.msg: Topic model: is:"topic" role (doc/roles.md) + nearest(role) walk already answers Topic/Meme abstraction directly - roles.md's own table rejects a TopicPage subclass and topic:true flag. columns() gives subtopics-as-columns; children: gives static composition; store() gives per-page persistent state keyed on url; declaring.md's directory.json+children verdict covers discovery/order/CMS question.

Subtopics/spaces: columns() (doc/columns.md) - six width words, default column, drag-resize, is-role cross-column messaging - is the subtopic/space mechanism; imagine/page.js is a live columns world; ext/Panel is chrome for wireframing arrangements, not a fit for user-created channels.

Omnibox/search: nothing close to a command palette exists. ux/Filter (segment+search driving a predicate) is the nearest primitive to extend. ux/Menu is a click menu, ext/Dropdown a picker popover - neither is type-ahead search. nav.js is a 5-link stub, looks vestigial. directory.json is a full generated site tree that could seed a client index. keydown handling exists ad hoc in Panel/Wizard/Tree/DevBar/editor/Ask - no shared keyboard layer.

Community/chat/writes: imagine/stream/ (stream.js + Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js) gives proven live multi-window JSONL sync at ~9ms over rpc:append; imagine/cms/ gives a working markdown edit+publish pipeline (rpc:write + Page.file()). Both run only over the loopback dev socket - nothing writes from a deployed static site today. ext/Ask is a Claude-only chat bridge, localhost-gated, not user chat.

Users/auth: notes/auth/readme.md is a full unbuilt design record (GitHub OAuth, signed HMAC cookie, D1 schema for users/likes/teams) - the strongest existing thinking. Server/plugins/Auth.js is real working code but Express-session + Google One-Tap on the DEV server, hardcoded session secret, violates the static-site-at-runtime constraint. ux/Auth is a login/signup/reset UI shell with no backend wiring.

Storage: ext/Saver (save/load/delete queue - FileSaver dev-only, LocalStorageSaver deployed, MemorySaver test) and ext/JSONL (append-only replay, the whole AI-log spine) are solid reusable primitives. core/Item+List give a persistent DOM-free tree (Panel's base). blog/posts.js is a hand-written manifest acting as content DB, with meta.mjs generating committed static derivatives. No multi-writer backend beyond the loopback dev socket.

Real-time: dev/Socket/doc/wire.md documents a full working protocol - one MCP HTTP hop plus one WebSocket, jsonl-tail streaming, eval - but it is loopback-gated to the dev server only (an RCE was closed on this exact gate, Server/readme.md). No production real-time transport (no Durable Object, no WebSocket path) exists outside localhost.

Video: imagine/youtube/ (Player wrapper + Cues timeline engine over the IFrame API) and imagine/feeds/video/ (lazy poster+click iframe) cover playback/embedding well and are reused already by the 3D pager tour. Nothing exists for upload, YouTube auth, or transcript/chapter import.

AI: ext/Ask (browser-to-Claude bridge, localhost only) and ext/Research (append-only credence-graded research program, CLI+MCP writers, live pages) are real and strong - Research's claim/vote/verdict shape is a directly reusable model for AI-assisted wiki/topic-creation workflows. Server/plugins/MCP.js and Research.js expose dev-only tools, not user-facing AI. fal.ai: zero references anywhere in the framework (grepped) - fully missing.

Levels/badges/progression: no dedicated system or UI component in ui/ or ux/. imagine/game/page.js and imagine/team/page.js both build progress tracking from is:"topic" + this.store() (rooms found/items carried; kanban lanes/points) - that role+store combo is exactly the primitive a levels system would extend, but there is no badge, XP or certification concept anywhere.

Publishing/deploy: wrangler.jsonc already configures Cloudflare Workers assets serving public/ with SPA fallback; root readme.md documents automatic per-branch preview deploys. blog/meta.mjs (manifest -> committed static derivatives: meta shells, feed, sitemap) is a directly reusable pattern for topic publishing. No worker/ code, D1, DO, KV or R2 exists yet - deploy today is 100% static assets, nothing dynamic.

Two counts (grep, verbatim from the brief): extends Page = 24 hits across public - live subclasses Section, ErrorPage, Doc, Post, AITask, Research, Program, Shell, Screen, Deck, Scene, Article, BlogxSwapPart(Part), Blog, plus Complete/Guarded/Reachable/Sealed/Honest in core/new/1 (a dead, non-live snapshot per core/readme.md), plus 3 quoted mentions inside doc strings (not real classes). is: role = 6 hits: roles used are topic (5x: game, team, columns/uses/split, columns/uses/inbox, columns/refs) and document (1x: columns/refs).

Topic-abstraction recommendation: is:"topic" role, not a Topic-extends-Page subclass and not plain config. core/Page/doc/roles.md already argued and settled this exact question (2026-08-27): a subclass forces a file per role and shadows the very accessor it defines (a TopicPage's own this.topic() would be itself); a topic:true flag shadows this.topic() on the page that claims it; is: + nearest(role) finds a role at any depth through columns/panels with zero registry and zero import cycle. Plain config isn't a real third option - a topic's extra fields (store(), levels, spaces) are just page.js fields already; is: is what turns that config into a relationship other pages can discover without importing it.

Verified headless (private server, PORT=8093, killed on landing): /imagine/platform/existing/ renders at 1280 and 3440 - table (12 rows), no console/page errors, no document-level horizontal overflow, table compresses inside .ac("wide") rather than overflowing its column prose. Screenshots confirm clean wrapping at both widths.

assign.outcome:
**Scouted all 11 platform concerns against the existing framework — table plus the topic-abstraction call, landed.** [Existing framework](/imagine/platform/existing/) — reuse as-is: topic model, subtopics/columns, storage primitives, video embedding, static publishing. Extend: community/writes (proven but dev-socket-only), real-time (same), AI (Research's shape reuses well), publishing (static half done, zero dynamic Worker/D1/DO code). Missing: Omnibox/search, a deployable users/auth backend, levels/badges/progression as a system.

**Topic abstraction: `is: "topic"` role** — [`core/Page/doc/roles.md`](/framework/core/Page/doc/roles/) already argued and settled this exact question in 2026-08-27 against the same two alternatives the brief names, and rejected both. Not a third option: "plain config" already lives on the page literal — `is:` is what makes it discoverable.

**The two counts, verified against the brief's own greps:** `extends Page` = 24 hits (14 live classes, 7 in a dead `core/new/1/` snapshot, 3 quoted mentions). `is: "…"` role = 6 hits (`topic` ×5, `document` ×1).

Left for the mastermind: wiring `existing` into [`/imagine/platform/`](/imagine/platform/)'s `children:` — this task's fence forbade editing that file.
